To find the number of triangles that can be formed using the vertices of a regular dodecagon, we need to choose 3 vertices out of the 12 available vertices. This can be done using combinations.

The number of ways to choose 3 vertices out of 12 is given by the combination formula:
\[ \binom{12}{3} = \frac{12!}{3!(12-3)!} = \frac{12 \times 11 \times 10}{3 \times 2 \times 1} = 220 \]

Therefore, there are $\boxed{220}$ triangles that can be formed using the vertices of a regular dodecagon.

grade.gold_answer: No three vertices are collinear, so any combination of 3 vertices will make a triangle. Choosing 3 out of 12 is $\binom{12}{3}=\boxed{220}.$
